one_liner: Rust bioinformatics format libraries; noodles-fasta builds samtools-compatible .fai indexes about 6x faster than samtools faidx.
what_it_does: noodles is a family of Rust crates for BAM, CRAM, SAM, VCF/BCF, BGZF, FASTA, FASTQ, GFF/GTF, tabix and related formats, usable one by one or through the noodles meta crate with per-format features. The catalogued claim is noodles-fasta's indexer: fasta::fs::index(path) returns an fai::Index, and fai::fs::write writes the same five-column .fai that samtools faidx produces; the io::Indexer type works over any BufRead. It is a library, not a CLI: the benchmarked binary is a small wrapper written by the z-fasta author that calls those two functions.
how_it_is_fast: The indexer reads through a BufReader and finds line ends with memchr (SIMD-accelerated byte search) on each buffered chunk, counting a whole line's bases at once and only checking the first byte of each line for '>'. HTSlib 1.24's fai_build_core, which samtools faidx uses, instead pulls every byte through bgzf_getc into a per-character state machine that also tests each byte with isgraph/isspace and inserts names into a hash table to reject duplicates. The samtools build in the comparison is the upstream default -O2 with a shared libhts, and the scaling table suggests roughly 15 ms of fixed samtools startup against about 3.5 ms for the noodles wrapper (derived from page data).
when_to_use: Rust pipelines that need to build or read .fai indexes of large, uniformly wrapped FASTA (genomes, transcriptomes) without shelling out to samtools.
Batch indexing of many reference or assembly files where samtools' per-file start-up and byte-at-a-time scan dominate (about 2.2 GB/s against 0.37 GB/s on GRCh38, warm cache).
Projects that already use noodles for BAM, CRAM or VCF and want one consistent, MIT-licensed Rust dependency for reference handling.
Low-memory environments: peak RSS was 3.6 MiB on the genome against 9.3 MiB for samtools.
when_not_to_use: FASTA with ragged line widths, trailing whitespace or mixed LF/CRLF endings: the indexer rejects them (as samtools does); a lenient tool such as z-fasta's .zfi mode is needed.

bgzip-compressed FASTA: fs::index opens the file as plain text and writes no .gzi, while samtools faidx indexes BGZF FASTA directly; region queries on bgzipped FASTA were also far slower than samtools in issue #146 (12.8 s against 0.024 s before PR #147 in 2023, still about 10x slower after it).
You need a command-line tool: noodles ships examples, not a supported faidx binary, and its README calls the API experimental.
Maximum indexing speed: in the same benchmark the Zig z-fasta indexer is about 3.6x faster than noodles on the genome.

integration.form: crate (noodles-fasta 0.67.0, or the noodles meta crate with the fasta feature)
integration.dependencies: bstr, memchr, noodles-bgzf, noodles-core; tokio only with the async feature
integration.platforms: any platform Rust supports (pure Rust; memchr picks SIMD paths at run time)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the Indexer owns its reader and is used from one thread
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — writes a samtools-compatible .fai for well-formed uncompressed FASTA, but it is a library call, not the samtools faidx CLI, and does not handle bgzipped input or .gzi files

gotchas: Output parity with samtools was never checked for noodles: the z-fasta report's byte comparison of .fai files covers only z-fasta, and its messy-FASTA table records exit codes, not output.

Semantics differ at the edges: HTSlib counts only isgraph characters as bases, warns and keeps the first of duplicate sequence names, and skips whitespace after '>'; noodles counts every byte of a line except a trailing CR and has no duplicate-name check in the indexer code read.
The small-file ratios are mostly process start-up (1 MiB: 3.7 ms against 17.5 ms); the asymptotic gap is about 7x per MiB.
noodles' API is versioned 0.x and changes often (fasta 0.66.0 was measured, 0.67.0 is current), so pin versions.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among the bioinformatics siblings (mosdepth for depth, sambamba and mako against samtools view/sort, rasusa for subsampling), noodles is the one to pick when you need a Rust library rather than a finished command-line tool, here for FASTA indexing; pick z-fasta instead when raw indexing speed or tolerance of messy FASTA matters more than a broad format library.
verified_claims_summary: An independent benchmark in the z-fasta repository (zebrac v0.6.2, 5 samples after 3 warmups, warm cache, AMD Ryzen 9 3950X per the z-fasta README) timed 'rm -f x.fai; tool index x' for a noodles-fasta 0.66.0 wrapper (cargo release profile, rustc version not stated) and samtools 1.24 faidx (HTSlib 1.24, default -O2, compiler not stated): GRCh38 primary assembly 1.364 s against 8.161 s (about 6.0x), GENCODE v46 transcripts 0.411 s against 1.711 s (about 4.2x), UniProt human proteome 0.018 s against 0.065 s (about 3.7x).
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-10-08), MIT-licensed and widely used (727 stars, about 485k noodles-fasta downloads), but still a 0.x API that its author calls experimental.
